title: Light & dark theme modes
description: Optional visitor light/dark toggle, dual palettes in admin, and data-theme CSS variables — not enabled by default.

blocks.text: By default every template ships a single light-oriented palette in SITE.theme.colors and the admin Theme & Colors tab edits that palette only. The theme-modes optional core module adds a second dark palette, a public toggle, and [data-theme="dark"] CSS variable overrides so visitors can switch without breaking Tailwind semantic tokens (bg-primary, text-text-main, etc.).

blocks.title: Not installed by default
blocks.text: Hotel, real-estate, and dev-agency templates do not include theme-modes unless you add it with tempjs add-module or pnpm template:add-module. Templates that are dark-styled only (e.g. dev-agency) can still use theme-modes to offer a light mode alongside the dark palette.
Run from a generated client project root (with .tempjs.json):

blocks.code:
tempjs add-module theme-modes
pnpm prisma db push   # no-op if no new models — safe to run
pnpm dev

pnpm template:add-module dev-agency theme-modes
pnpm dev:dev-agency

items: Adds theme.appearance (default system) and theme.colorsDark to constants/site.ts
Wires ThemeModeInit in app/layout.tsx (FOUC-safe beforeInteractive script)
Adds suppressHydrationWarning on <html> and <body> (docsite hydration pattern)
Removes inline SITE.theme.colors styles on <html> when present (hotel template) so CSS vars can switch
Extends admin Theme & Colors tab with Light / Dark palette editors and default appearance selector

blocks.title: Avoid hydration errors
blocks.text: Match the docsite pattern: (1) ThemeModeInit with strategy="beforeInteractive" sets data-theme and color-scheme on <html> before React hydrates. (2) suppressHydrationWarning on both <html> and <body> in app/layout.tsx — the installer adds these automatically. (3) ThemeModeToggle renders a placeholder until mount, then reads data-theme from the DOM (never localStorage during SSR). Do not set data-theme from React state on the root layout without these guards.

Although the theme-modes module configures the root layout and global styles automatically, you must manually mount the toggle component in your project's header or navigation bar. It is not placed automatically to avoid cluttering your bespoke design.
Step 1: Locate your Header or Navbar Component
Open your main header/navigation component (e.g. app/components/Header.tsx or app/components/Navbar.tsx). This is typically where visitors expect to find the light/dark mode controls.
Step 2: Import and Mount the Toggle
Import the ThemeModeToggle component and place it inside your header row. The component is fully typed and accepts classNames for positioning:

Start your development server (pnpm dev) and click the toggle button. You should see the HTML data attribute update to data-theme="dark" or data-theme="light", and the global tailwind variable colors shift to reflect your colorsDark values from constants/site.ts.
Visitor choice is stored in localStorage (tempjs-theme-mode). First visit uses theme.appearance from site.ts (system, light, or dark) before fallback to system preferences.
